reason: This text fragment (Exodus 19) addresses preparation for God's revelation at Mount Sinai and regulations about who can approach the sacred mountain, not the question of who is permitted to offer sacrifices. While the passage mentions priests (הַכֹּהֲנִים) must sanctify themselves when approaching God, and discusses restrictions on who can ascend the mountain, it makes no statement whatsoever about sacrificial offerings or any exclusive priestly right to present sacrifices to Yahweh. The passage focuses on physical boundaries, sanctification requirements, and the structured access permitted to Moses, Aaron, the elders, and the people—not on sacrifice.
